P: Preliminary; PR: Partially Revised
  • India’s current account deficit (CAD) widened from 5.4 per cent in Q2 to a record high of 6.7 per cent of GDP in Q3, driven mainly by larger trade deficit.

  • As net invisibles moderated, CAD rose by over 61 per cent to US$ 32.6 billion (6.7 per cent of GDP) in Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 20.2 billion (4.4 per cent of GDP) in the corresponding quarter, 2011-12.

    • As net invisibles moderated, CAD rose by over 61 per cent to US$ 32.6 billion (6.7 per cent of GDP) in Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 20.2 billion (4.4 per cent of GDP) in the corresponding quarter, 2011-12.

    However, with the surge in capital inflows, CAD during the quarter could be fully financed. The pickup in capital flows was mainly due to foreign portfolio investment which rose to US$ 8.6 billion during Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 1.8 billion in Q3 of previous year. While loans availed by banks and corporate sector amounted to US$ 7.1 billion, net Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) declined to US$ 2.5 billion in Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 5 billion in the corresponding quarter of 2011-12.

  • During April-December 2012, CAD stood at US$ 71.7 billion accounting for 5.4 per cent of GDP as against US$ 56.5 billion (4.1 per cent of GDP) in the same period of 2011.

    • During April-December 2012, CAD stood at US$ 71.7 billion accounting for 5.4 per cent of GDP as against US$ 56.5 billion (4.1 per cent of GDP) in the same period of 2011.

    Current Account Balance

  • Widening trade deficit led to worsening of CAD to US$ 32.6 billion (6.7 per cent of GDP) in Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 22.6 billion (5.4 per cent of GDP) in the previous quarter and US$ 20.2 billion (4.4 per cent) in Q3 of 2011-12.

    • Widening trade deficit led to worsening of CAD to US$ 32.6 billion (6.7 per cent of GDP) in Q3 of 2012-13 from US$ 22.6 billion (5.4 per cent of GDP) in the previous quarter and US$ 20.2 billion (4.4 per cent) in Q3 of 2011-12.

  • During April-December 2012, CAD widened both in absolute terms as well as a proportion of GDP reflecting mainly burgeoning trade deficit. The CAD in April-December 2012 at US$ 71.7 billion was 5.4 per cent of GDP as compared with US$ 56.5 billion (4.1 per cent of GDP) in April-December 2011.
